Hyperprolactinemia

“We can’t tell anyone” yes you can, don’t isolate yourselves!

I see a lot of posts of people sharing a pregnancy anonymously on reddit thinking they can’t tell anyone before the 12 week mark.

You absolutely can tell people, and I would recommend it for most people but ESPECIALLY for those who are going through this for the first time.

You don’t have to tell everyone, you don’t have to make a full announcement. But you can tell a few people if you WANT to

Yes, there’s always a chance of miscarriage, and you don’t want to be yelling things from the rooftops only to then have every neighbor and their cousin asking you five months down the line how things are going if there was a devastating loss.

However, if you and your partner DO go through a devastating and emotional loss, are you planning to carry through completely isolated with outside help?

You shouldn’t! That is psychological torture, worst of all, it is completely self imposed

Please tell your friends, have a group of people who you tell right away. You each need someone to talk to about this who isn’t your partner, or else you will go stir crazy.

Tell some of your closest friends, tell closest family, tell people you can trust to be discrete as things progress

But please tell SOMEONE, I promise, it is going to feel good for you to share the news with them and they will love to share the joy with you

And if something bad does happen? Then those same loved ones will be there to love and support you through it as well :)

Pregnancy is hard enough, don’t isolate yourself, enjoy it and share that joy with others :)

Fast forward to now - we’ve been trying again, and I’ve been tracking everything closely with ovulation tests. On 12th June, when my period was due, I got a faint line on a pregnancy test and continued testing daily for the next week. All were faint positives, and I had symptoms like sore breasts, nausea, and acid reflux.

Then on Sunday 22nd, I started spotting, which quickly turned into bleeding and severe cramps. The tests were negative, and I panicked. I called the EPU the next day and they booked me in for a scan on the Tuesday but when I got there, they wouldn’t do it because my test was negative. I saw a nurse who took bloods to check my HCG, and she said the levels were so low it wouldn’t indicate a pregnancy. She mentioned I could possibly be referred for further testing (even though it’s usually after 3 miscarriages, my hospital might offer it after 2).

What’s been really hard is feeling dismissed as I had consistent positives and physical symptoms for days, but I was left feeling like it had all been in my head. On top of that, this current bleeding doesn’t feel like any period I’ve had before.

Sorry for the long message but I just wondered if anyone else has experienced something similar?

I wanted to briefly share my experience, in hopes it might help encourage someone else now or sometime in the future. 

I recently experienced my first miscarriage, a MMC. We had our first ultrasound at 9 weeks, 3 days. Our little one was only measuring 7 weeks and 3 days. There was no heart beat. 

Obviously we were so sad about this news. That appointment was a blur, and just basically by default, I chose the option of expectant management. I wanted time to process my emotions, and I knew I could always make a different decision if needed. I guess deep down, I also still held out some hope maybe they were wrong and everything would be ok. I realize that was just part of trying to process the grief. 

I scheduled another appointment for two weeks later and went home to wait. Those two weeks were two of the most difficult weeks of my life. The waiting, the fear of how and when things would start, fear of being to far away from home, just in case. Every time I looked down, I knew our baby was still with me, but no longer developing or growing. It was just a very difficult time. I had lots of cramping, but no spotting. I kept thinking, "this is it, it's starting", but it didn't. That was also very frustrating to go from praying you don't start spotting when you think your baby is still healthy and growing, to being disappointed you're not spotting because you just want to get the process over with. 

I went to my appointment after the two weeks. I discussed everything with the doctor, and also mentioned we had a short weekend trip coming up that I was really thinking of canceling because I was worried about the process beginning while out of town. She listened intently, the basically just said, "I think given everything I'm hearing you say, and the fact that it's been 4 weeks since the baby passed, your best option would be a D&C. Why don't we schedule it for Thursday?" That was only 2 days later. Immediately when she said that, I felt like 1000 pounds were lifted off my shoulders and the noise that had been constant in my head and heart since we received the news about our baby finally calmed. I knew right away, even though I hadn't truly considered this option previously, that it was the right thing to do. We scheduled the procedure.

I called the after hours nurses line, and they told me what to watch out for, but said to come in for my procedure anyway, no matter what, so they could monitor me and make sure the process was complete.

I called my midwife again, and she ordered HCG tests. Thankfully, the numbers looked great. That reassured me… again, for maybe a day.

At 8 weeks, I had another ultrasound—and this time we saw the baby’s heartbeat! Such a relief. My midwife said I might just be a “bleeder” and advised us to hold off on sex for a bit since that could have been a trigger. I finally feel like I can enjoy the pregnancy.

Of course, sometimes spotting can be a sign of something more serious. But in my case—and in many others I’ve read about—it turned out to be just one of those scary, weird symptoms of early pregnancy.
